Blech club night ticket

A Designers Republic ticket for the Warp Records club night Blech, mixing manga, Japanese katakana, coded labels, and LCD-style type.

Context

The V&A holds the ticket as E.50-2022, titled “Blech”, by The Designers Republic, UK, 1996–7, given by The Designers Republic. V&A E.50-2022.

Wikipedia says The Designers Republic is sometimes associated with popularizing the Y2K look. Wikipedia: Y2K aesthetic.

Observed

  • The ground is flat lime green. A large manga-style face with huge blue eyes, white highlights, and freckles fills the lower two thirds.
  • The heading “BLECH:” is in heavy orange-red sans-serif capitals, followed by katakana in bright blue.
  • A purple-edged box holds “BL-3CH” in a dotted, LCD-like pixel face; next to it are outlined rounded pictogram characters.
  • Small type reads “FORMAT: DISCOCLUB PASS”, “ADMITS ONE. PRICE £4.00”, and “THIS TICKET VALID MAY 11 ONLY” in magenta.
  • A pink double-headed arrow at right carries “WARNING! THIS PASS MUST BE SURRENDERED ON ENTRY” set vertically, and a small round “DR” badge sits at top right.

Why it belongs

The ticket treats a club pass like a product label from a Japanese future: format codes, model numbers, warnings, and trademark signs. This coded-label habit is the graphic side of the style’s “interface as device” layout.

It shows the flat, bright end of Y2K graphics before gloss and chrome became common in print.

Borrow

Add fake model codes, format labels, and warnings in small capitals around a main image.

Set a short code in a dotted LCD face inside a thin outlined box.

Mix Latin headings with a second script or pictograms as texture.
